column1: # Muscle Bomber / Saturday Night Slam Masters (CPS1.5 `slammast`) ARRANGE
# trigger map -- *** BUILT: work/packs/mbomber_arrange.cpk ***
#   arcade QSound sound-command  ->  FM Towns "Muscle Bomber: The Body
#   Explosion" (1994, Capcom) CD-DA arrange track.
# STATUS: arena-theme rows EAR-CONFIRMED; loop points proposed, not yet confirmed.
#   * PACK-WORTHINESS: **CONFIRMED** by user ear verdict -- all 5 A/B pairs in
#     the internal listening archive were judged to match AND to be arranged.
#   * The arcade cmd->scene side is HARD-grounded: manifests/protocol/slammast.json
#     plus internal campaign notes, every music label tied
#     to a same-run MAME snapshot (venue cards and named health bars) and to the
#     0xff00/0xff06 control bracketing.
#   * The mapping law 0x0021+N <-> tr15+N is **VALIDATED AT 5 OF 9 POINTS** by
#     that had rested on the law rather than on its own statistics.  The
#     remaining four rows follow by exhaustion: 9 long tracks tr15-tr23 map to
#     9 commands 0x0021-0x0029, exactly.
#   * LOOP POINTS: ear-confirmed, manifests/mbomber_arrange_loops.tsv.
#   * BUILT: pack/build_mbomber.py -> work/packs/mbomber_arrange.cpk (94.8 MB,
#     9 tracks, 9 play triggers) and mra/CPS+/Saturday Night Slam Masters
#     (Arrange).mra on jtcps15_cpsplus.  The builder accepts ONLY rows whose
#     confidence is `confirmed` or `by_exhaustion`, so the two `low` rows below
#     are deliberately NOT in the pack.
# SOURCE QUALIFIES ON IDENTITY (this is settled, see PREP_NOTES.md):
#   The FM Towns CD-DA is a genuine distinct ARRANGEMENT (Setsuo Yamamoto), not
#   a render of the arcade QSound master.  Drift-immune windowed waveform test:
#   same-master control r_med 0.90/0.67, different-theme control r_med 0.22/0.19,
#   arcade-vs-FM-Towns probes r_med 0.25/0.23/0.22/0.18 -- at the negative floor.
#   So this source does NOT hit the render exclusion that dropped SFA3, Pocket
#   Fighter, Darkstalkers and Warriors of Fate.
# DIALECT NOTE (cps15_qsound): CPS1.5 uses the CPS2 QSound shared-RAM RECORD
#   protocol relocated to latch page 0xf18000 -- NOT the CPS1 byte latch.  A
#   record is a run of odd-offset byte writes (cmd_hi 0x01, cmd_lo 0x03, args
#   0x05..0x19) terminated by the 0x1f handshake write; the Z80 acks 0xff at
#   0xc00f.  Pack suppression must therefore be a per-COMMAND music filter on
#   the assembled 16-bit command, applied at the handshake, not a byte filter.
#   Swallow only the mapped BGM commands; pass the whole SFX/voice space
#   (0x00a0-0x01e8 and the low SFX/voice commands 0x0010, 0x0030-0x0072) through
#   untouched.  Keep the control family 0xff00 (stop) / 0xff06 (fade) as the
#   MSU/CD stop and fade hooks -- 0xff06 fires ~60 frames before 0xff00 at every
#   demo-match end, which is the natural fade window.
# LOOP AUTHORING (PROPOSED, AWAITING EAR): the CD-DA tracks are FADE MASTERS
#   with NO embedded loop points, exactly like the SFA1 arrange source, and they
#   contain no digitally exact internal repeats (they are live re-recordings),
#   so loops had to be authored rather than recovered.  Loop points for all nine
#   arena themes are now proposed in `manifests/mbomber_arrange_loops.tsv`, with
#   full-context previews in `the internal listening archive`.  Loop lengths run
#   40.2-72.2 s; 6 of 9 want the equal-power hardware crossfade (XFADE_N = 7200
#   samples, ~163 ms), 3 take a hard cut.  Samples are 44100 Hz stereo frame
#   indices into cd_full/trNN.wav.  The short cues (0x0039, 0x0058) are one-shot
#   and need no loop.
# Columns follow manifests/ffight_arrange_trigger_map.tsv:
#   cmd
